issue.title: test_prepare_pytest_tmpdir_leak_does_not_break_a_later_scratch_read times out under the full parallel lane, passes in isolation
issue.description:
Found by the sase-zl.13.11 landing gate (just check-full, monitor yq3nkkcww4vv, master 3781cd264c, 2026-09-13): the node failed with `_pytest.pytester.Pytester.TimeoutExpired: 60 second timeout expired` while the full parallel lane was saturated (16 xdist workers; sibling tests clocked 30-145s, and this node's own passing runs have clocked 60.32s in slowest-durations). A re-run of the same node on the unchanged, idle tree passed in 5.3s.

Mechanism: the test drives `pytester.runpytest_subprocess(..., timeout=60)` for an inner pytest run of three collected nodes (test_run_pytest_tmpdir.py::test_prepare_pytest_tmpdir_honors_override, test_run_pytest_health.py::test_scoped_run_lands_in_the_durable_health_store, tests/ace/tui/widgets/test_artifact_ref_completion_catalog.py::test_commit_completion_rows_match_shared_inventory_and_resolve). The 60s budget is a fixed wall-clock bound that the inner interpreter start + collection + the TUI widgets node cannot reliably meet while the outer lane is saturated. Likely remediations: raise/scale the timeout, shrink the inner node set, or serialize the node — worker's judgment.

Not caused by sase-zl.13.11 (its commits touch monitor/continuation code only; the fixture change in tests/monitor/_supervise.py stamps metadata and does not affect this test).
